header.title: Clousight Bench
board.title: Results
board.empty: Nothing measured yet. Run `csbench run` and this page fills in.
suite.compare_blurb: The latest run on each platform. Bold marks the current leader on a metric whose direction we know.
record.headline: What it found
record.trust_blurb: What was run, by which evaluator, over which dataset — the chain that makes this result checkable.
record.suite_version_blurb: Pins the dataset and harness. When this changes, results before and after are not directly comparable.
record.evaluator_blurb: The scorer that turned raw evidence into these numbers. `official` means it is the suite's recognised evaluator — a statement of provenance, not an audit.
record.dataset_blurb: A hash of exactly which data was used. Two runs sharing it ran over identical input.
record.artifacts_blurb: The raw evidence this verdict was computed from, kept on disk beside the record.
record.sha_blurb: Content hash — proves the file has not changed since the run sealed it.
record.no_measurements_blurb: The machinery ran and the stages passed; the evaluator returned nothing to report. Check the trace before treating this as a result.
items.title: Per-item detail
items.filter_hint: Filter by item id or group
items.none: This benchmark produced no per-item detail.
items.none_blurb: Suites like TPC-H measure an engine as a whole; their evidence is in the execution trace and the artifacts.
items.artifact_blurb: Not inlined — fetch it from the artifacts directory beside the record.
items.status.ok_blurb: A real result: this item passed.
items.status.fail_blurb: A real result: this item did not pass.
items.status.skip_blurb: Not scored — absent from the aggregate, and not a failure.
items.status.error_blurb: The scorer itself failed here. This is our bug, not the subject's.
metric.official_blurb: Emitted by the benchmark's recognised evaluator. A statement of provenance, not an external audit.
metric.unknown_blurb: No written description for this key, so it is shown as recorded and no direction is claimed.
engineer.toggle_blurb: Show fingerprints, identity and environment — the fields that make a run reproducible.
engineer.title: Engineer view
engineer.blurb: Everything the pages above leave out. Nothing here is needed to read a result; all of it is needed to reproduce one.
engineer.fingerprints_blurb: Two runs sharing a fingerprint measured the same thing the same way. A difference tells you which part moved.
engineer.identity_blurb: Which benchmark, which platform, and which versions of each produced this record.
engineer.environment_blurb: Where it ran. Environment-dependent numbers are only comparable across matching environments.
engineer.extensions_blurb: Namespaced extras carried by the record, including the trace id linking it to its spans.
live.idle_hint: Start a run in a terminal — `csbench run --domain … --benchmark …` — and it appears here on its own.
live.no_intermediate_progress: no progress reported from inside a measured window
live.metrics_blurb: Computed in the browser from the steps finished so far. These are not the run's measurements — those are decided after it ends.
live.finished: This run has finished and its record is sealed.
live.dropped: Some live events were dropped to stay within limits ({summary}). The sealed record is unaffected.
list.title: All runs
detail.title: Record
trace.title: Execution trace
timeline.include_track: Include this track in the selection
timeline.zoom_hint: Drag to zoom into a time window; W/S zoom, A/D pan, Backspace goes back
trace.source.full_blurb: The run's lifecycle stages with the benchmark's own spans nested inside the stage that produced them.
trace.source.artifact_blurb: The benchmark's own trajectory. Recorded before the lifecycle and the benchmark's spans were merged, so the stages are not in this view.
trace.source.lifecycle_blurb: This run reported nothing finer than its lifecycle stages — every run has these.
trace.unaccounted_hint: how much, not when: the row model carries idle time as a total, so this segment's position is a convention
dock.empty: Select a span to see its detail.
section.suites_blurb: What can be measured: the benchmarks installed here, their pinned data and their evaluators.
section.targets_blurb: What can be pointed at: the managed cloud products this build has an adapter for, and how mature each adapter is.
section.runs_blurb: What happened: every run, its verdict, and the evidence under it.
section.observe_blurb: What is happening: runs in flight, and the execution traces they leave.
section.config_blurb: The vocabulary and the machine: metric definitions, installed plugins, environment.

config.title: Config
platform.none_blurb: A domain plugin supplies the adapters that reach a cloud product. `csbench list` shows what this build can see.
platform.status.reference_blurb: An offline stand-in. It runs without any cloud account and is what the test suites use.
platform.status.experimental_blurb: Reaches a real service. Proven end to end, but the adapter's surface may still change.
platform.status.skeleton_blurb: Wired but not yet proven against the vendor. An empty run count here means it cannot run yet, not that nobody tried.
target.title: Targets
target.blurb: What gets measured: an adapter plus the configuration that reaches one instance of it. One file each, under configs/.
target.readonly_notice: This viewer is read-only. Restart it with `csbench serve --allow-write` to create, edit or delete targets.
target.none_blurb: A target is one instance of a platform — where it is and how to reach it. Each one is a file under configs/, and `csbench run --config` takes it.
target.none_matching_blurb: Clear the filter to see every target.
target.contents_blurb: The file as it is on disk — comments, order and all.
target.redacted_blurb: The server did not send this file's text, so it cannot be edited here. These keys hold what looks like a credential; edit the file where the real value lives.
target.usage_blurb: A sealed record does not carry the config file its run was given, so runs started any other way are not counted here.
target.delete_confirm: Delete this target? The file is removed from disk. Runs that already used it are unaffected — they froze their own configuration.
target.unparsable: This file could not be read as a target.
target.name: Name
target.name_hint: The file will be configs/<name>.yaml, and `csbench run --config` takes that path. Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
target.yaml_hint: Two top-level keys: `target:` (where the platform is) and `params:` (what the benchmark should do). The server parses this before writing it.
target.err_name_charset: Only letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore — a name is not a path.
target.err_name_reserved: That name is a directory, not a file.
target.err_body_redacted: This text still holds the redaction placeholder ***. Saving it would overwrite the real credential.
target.overwrite_hint: Without this, saving over a target that already exists is refused.
run.new_blurb: One benchmark, one platform, one target. The run starts as a separate process and the live view opens on it.
run.section_what_blurb: The benchmark decides which data is used and which metrics come out; both are frozen into this run's configuration snapshot.
run.benchmark_hint: Its pinned dataset version travels with the result — the same benchmark id always means the same data.
run.domain_hint: Which family of platform this run is against. Changing it changes the platforms below.
run.platform_hint: `reference` runs offline and costs nothing. Anything else reaches a real service.
run.target_hint: The config that reaches one instance. A reference platform needs none.
run.section_params_blurb: Passed to the benchmark as --param key=value. Strings, numbers and booleans only; what each benchmark accepts is its own business.
run.section_exec_blurb: Repeats are aggregated into one plan; warmups run first and are excluded from the statistics.
run.repeat_hint: Measured repeats, at most {max}. The ceiling is what stops one click becoming an afternoon of billable work.
run.warmup_hint: Runs first, excluded from the statistics. At most {max}.
run.confirm_blurb: What this run will freeze that you did not type. The evaluator and the dataset digest are resolved by the run itself and appear in its configuration snapshot.
run.warn_skeleton: This adapter is a skeleton: wired, but not yet proven against the vendor. The run is likely to stop early.
run.warn_unseen: Nothing in this results directory has run this benchmark on this platform. That is not a rule against it — nothing in the registry pairs the two — but it has not been done here before.
run.warn_cost: This platform reaches a real service, so this run may cost real money.
run.readonly_notice: This viewer is read-only. Restart it with `csbench serve --allow-write` to start runs from here.
live.never_appeared: This run never reported any progress.
live.never_appeared_blurb: It was either never started, or it finished quickly enough that its progress directory has already been collected.
run.like_this_hint: Copies the benchmark, platform, target and parameters — not the repeat count.
config.metrics_blurb: What every measurement key means and which direction is an improvement. Defined in code; this is the reading of it.
config.plugins_blurb: Every registered extension point and what provides it. An empty kind is usually the answer to why something cannot run.
config.retired_blurb: Words this project used to use. If you met one in an old runbook, a commit message or a screenshot, this says what it became.
config.readonly_notice: None of this is editable from here: metric meanings and plugin wiring live in code, and a page that let you change them would be a page that lies.
suites.installed_blurb: What this build can measure: every benchmark it ships, the data each one is pinned to, and what can score it.
suites.no_evaluator: cannot be scored — no evaluator installed
